entries.title: 5 new Google Flow Tools designed by visual artists
entries.summary: Several squares with different icons related to filmmaking
entries.content:
Today, we're releasing five new tools that show how you can keep pushing the boundaries of visual storytelling in Google Flow, our AI creative studio. These five tools — all built by creatives — prove there’s increasingly no limit to what you can build in Google Flow. See how they can help you shape your next story, from concept to final cut.

1. Character Poster, by artist and filmmaker James Gerde

James Gerde treats his social feeds like curated galleries where visual consistency is everything. He built Character Poster to turn simple story concepts into polished, beautifully designed visuals. It helps creators maintain a signature style across their social stories — and can save hours of production work.

A cinematic “let’s go to the beach” poster generated with Character Poster by James Gerde.

2. Character Arc, by filmmaker and visual storyteller Anurag Tiwari

Anurag Tiwari built Character Arc to show how a character changes over time. It lets storytellers visualize the same character across different ages and life stages without losing their core look, speeding up character development before full production begins.

For his documentary “Children of the Sun,” which features present-day interviews with subjects reflecting on events from 1974, Anurag is using Character Arc to trace the protagonist’s life from childhood through adulthood.

"It helps me build his background while keeping him recognizable as the same person across different periods of the story," Anurag says.

A visual timeline of the protagonist generated with Character Arc for “Children of the Sun.”

3. Pixel Machine, also by Anurag Tiwari

Inspired by his love for retro digital aesthetics, Anurag also created Pixel Machine to give filmmakers and artists a playground that goes beyond polished AI visuals. It converts images into bitmap, ASCII, CRT, pixel art, and glitch styles, making it easier to design stylized title treatments, transitions, and music video visuals.

A stylized ASCII art animation and effects treatment, generated with Pixel Machine.

4. Lucid Glass, by artist and creative director Ezra Paulekas

Ezra Paulekas designed Lucid Glass to recreate the way light passes through glass, generating prisms, halos, refractions, and optical blooms. It works like an "impossible lens," giving photographers and filmmakers effects they could never capture with glass alone.

Pushing past the physical limitations of real-world lenses, generated with Lucid Glass.

5. Pocket Studio, by visual development artist and filmmaker Ryan McCoy

Drawing on more than two decades in previsualization and visual effects for major motion pictures, Ryan McCoy built Pocket Studio to turn everyday phone footage into more polished shots. From a single take, the tool generates multiple camera angles and upgrades the visual fidelity, all while keeping the actor’s original performance intact.

A polished multi-angle studio sequence generated with Pocket Studio.

Try these creative tools and build your own in Google Flow today.

entries.title: Google Search gets a major upgrade with Gemini 4 Hydrogen
entries.summary: Rotating carousel of cards with text "Gemini 4 Hydrogen" "Now in Google Search" and examples from the Google Search UI
entries.content:
Listen to article This content is generated by Google AI. Generative AI is experimental

Today, Google Search is bringing cutting-edge intelligence to everyone with Gemini 4 Hydrogen. This is the biggest model upgrade to Search yet.

Hydrogen is now available globally in Google Search for all users, delivering more helpful, visual, and intuitive responses with improved model capabilities:

  • Better understanding of intent: Search can now handle even more nuanced and complicated questions, quickly understanding what you need. Just ask in your natural flow of thought — including questions with multiple parts, hard-to-understand typos, or highly specific requests. With deeper instruction following and tool calling, Search more precisely follows what you want and gives you relevant responses that address each part of your question.
  • Improved query fan-out and linking: Hydrogen’s advanced reasoning supercharges our query fan-out technique in Search, connecting you to a broader range of helpful links than before. By more thoroughly understanding your question and conducting simultaneous queries across all the relevant subtopics, Search helps you find sites you previously might not have discovered.
  • More visual responses: You get highly adaptive, visual, and easy-to-scan responses that are uniquely relevant to your needs — at the speed of Search. You’ll see more images, structured responses, comparison tables, and custom tools built for you.
  • Richer language understanding: No matter what language you ask in, you’ll now get more highly nuanced and helpful responses across all supported AI Mode languages.

Try out Gemini 4 Hydrogen in Search today.

entries.title: Introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen
entries.summary: an image of carbon with the number 4 around it
entries.content:
Today, we’re introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen, bringing cutting-edge intelligence to everyone — with speed and efficiency for everyday coding and agentic workflows.

While our frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, excel at deep, long-horizon reasoning on your hardest problems, Hydrogen is built for rapid execution across diverse agentic workflows. With Hydrogen, we’re also bringing Gemini 4 to everyone — for all tiers of Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, the Gemini app, Google Search, and paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity.

Hydrogen surpasses Argon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its default high thinking level (51 vs. 50, and reaching 54 at its highest xhigh thinking setting), while often completing tasks faster than models in its class. Gemini 4 Hydrogen is priced flat across its entire 1 million-token context window at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens.

Unlocking efficiencies in multi-model workloads

In real-world software development, while teams rely on frontier models like Carbon and Argon for deep architectural judgment when designing systems or untangling subtle bugs, they still need a fast, disciplined execution model for writing code, running tests, and verifying changes. Hydrogen is built to stand on its own as a model for everyday work — or to pair with Carbon and Argon as the high-efficiency execution engine in multi-model workflows.

To help make this multi-model collaboration automatic, we’re introducing Orchestrator in Google Antigravity. Rather than using a single model from start to finish, Orchestrator dynamically switches between models like Carbon and Hydrogen within the same session. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Orchestrator reached near-Carbon task success rates while, on average, consuming 24% less quota and completing 19% faster. For workflows that require parallel agents, Carbon can act as the coordinator while Hydrogen can power worker and verifier agents to build and test changes simultaneously across isolated workspaces — helping teams ship complex projects faster without driving up token costs.

Scaling developer and enterprise workflows

Beyond multi-model workflows, Hydrogen is a major standalone upgrade for teams migrating from Gemini 3.8 Flash. It delivers significant leaps in both speed and intelligence — finishing tasks 2.5 times faster at its high default setting while more than tripling Terminal-Bench 4.1 scores (57% vs. 18.2%), cutting fabricated claims by more than 5x, and adapting cleanly when a tool call fails or a search returns empty. It also matches or outperforms competing models in its class across core developer and enterprise workflows:

  • Iterative repository coding and debugging: Hydrogen handles issue resolution, debugging, rapid iteration, and codebase Q&A with focused, surgical edits — delivering cleaner, production-ready code without rewriting unrelated files. It outperforms similar-tier models on SWE-sweep where it has to discover and repair bugs without breaking existing code. To explore large repositories efficiently, the model excels at natively batching file-read and search calls in parallel rather than inspecting files one by one; in early testing across complex graphs, SQL, and data-heavy enterprise workflows, our partners have seen Hydrogen run 2x to 2.8x faster while reducing token usage by 12% to 23%, compared to 3.8 Flash.
  • Open-ended agentic execution: On multi-step tasks like deep research, data analysis, and broad codebase navigation, Hydrogen ranks #5 on Agent Arena, arena.ai’s live benchmark. For deep domain reasoning and analysis, it leads its class on HLE-Diamond (58.8%), ranks #1 overall on Vals Tax Agent Bench (52.3%), ties for #1 on the Vals Legal Research Bench (55.8%), and leads its class on AutomationBench-AA.
  • Multimodal knowledge work: Hydrogen pairs native 1 million-token input with up to 1 million output tokens to synthesize dense PDFs, spreadsheets, charts, audio, and recorded video into polished, cited reports and structured deliverables. It outperforms other models on the new Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark (53.4%) for end-to-end agentic knowledge work over complex visual files, and on Agents’ Last Exam v1.1 (71.6%) for end-to-end professional workflows.
  • Web development: On tasks where speed matters to developers, like live UI prototyping, design-to-code iteration, and interactive app building, Hydrogen generates more functional, feature-complete layouts in fewer prompts.

Adaptable speed and intelligence across four thinking levels

We built Gemini 4 Hydrogen for real-world usability. Hydrogen’s four thinking levels — low, medium, high (default), and a new xhigh tier — offer a wide range of options across quality, latency, and cost, scaling in a smooth, predictable progression so you only wait and pay for the reasoning depth a task requires. Across thinking levels, Hydrogen matches or outperforms some of the competing models in its class while often finishing tasks faster and using fewer output tokens.

Fast, everyday help in the Gemini app and Search

For consumers, Gemini 4 Hydrogen makes it easier to get things done, staying on track and following instructions more closely across multi-turn conversations.

In the Gemini app, Hydrogen makes your everyday assistant even more helpful — it’s better at following your guidance, calling the right tools, and getting you to a reliable output with less back-and-forth.

  • Ready-to-go writing, research, and everyday work: Hydrogen sticks closely to your tone, format, and specific rules, so email drafts, study guides, rewrites, and documents come back ready to use on the first try. When you are comparing products or synthesizing dense material, it pulls together clear tables and visual breakdowns without dropping key details.
  • Connects the dots and gets more tasks done: Hydrogen breaks down your goal step-by-step, pulling relevant context from your uploads, Google apps like Gmail and Google Drive, and Connected Apps like Airtable and Dropbox. When you start a task in Gemini, it also more frequently calls the right tools and skills for the job, helping save you time as you check things off your to-do list.
  • Everyday prototyping and iteration: For exploring and testing ideas, Hydrogen generates clean, working layouts in fewer prompts, making it easy to prototype and refine interactive projects quickly, like synthesizing real-time global lightning strike data into an interactive 3D globe.

Hydrogen is significantly upgrading Search, delivering more helpful, intuitive responses for all users globally.

  • Better understands your true intent: With Hydrogen, you can ask your question in your natural flow of thought — even if you have multiple parts to your query, hard-to-understand typos, or highly specific requests — and Search will intelligently comprehend what you’re looking for.
  • More visual responses: You’ll get highly adaptive, visual, and easy-to-scan responses that are uniquely relevant to your needs, at the speed you expect from Search.
  • Wider range of relevant links: With Hydrogen’s advanced reasoning, we’re also upgrading our query fan-out technique in Search, connecting you to a broader range of helpful links than before, helping you find sites you previously might not have discovered.

Designed for safe, dependable execution at scale

Gemini 4 Hydrogen brings improvements from our latest Gemini 4 safety and security stack to our broadest audience yet, combining built-in training with real-time surface safeguards to help mitigate both misalignment and misuse. Beyond foundational protections, we focused on two areas that matter most for a faster model that’s for everyday work:

  • Safe, aligned, and secure agentic workflows: While 3.8 Flash has strong alignment and safeguards, Hydrogen is a leap ahead. It reduces overreach in agentic tasks by up to 81% and under-service by up to 79%, and cuts misaligned actions and task shortcutting across tool-use and coding evaluations by 12x. When faced with impossible or blocked tasks, it is up to 2x less likely to bypass permission boundaries and achieves a 96.7% honesty rate on our internal agent honesty evaluation.

    Building on our commitment toreasoning transparency, Hydrogen also preserves 99.9% chain-of-thought legibility with zero deceptive reasoning edits across more than 200,000 audited turns. Against indirect prompt injection attacks, Hydrogen is more than 2.3x more resilient on the Gray Swan IPI benchmark, while significantly improving robustness across tool use, computer use, and coding agents.
  • Helpful, reliable everyday interactions: Across our product surfaces, we tuned Hydrogen to make everyday conversations more reliable and safe. Our updated safeguards are also much more precise at distinguishing between real biosecurity risks and legitimate medical or scientific questions — keeping false refusals on HealthBench Pro under 0.4%.

For more details see the Gemini 4 Hydrogen model card.

Gemini 4 Hydrogen, available to everyone today

Starting today, Hydrogen is rolling out globally across our developer, enterprise, and consumer surfaces:

  • For developers: Build with the Gemini API in AI Studio and Android Studio, try it in AI Studio and if you’re a paid Google AI Pro or Ultra subscriber, you can try it in Google Antigravity.
  • For enterprises: Deploy it in Gemini for business via the API or model drop down, Google Antigravity, and in Gemini in Google Sheets for eligible business subscriptions.
  • For everyone: Start using it in the Gemini app model drop down 1 and in Google Search for all users, and in Gemini in Google Sheets starting with Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers.

entries.title: Scientists are using Google AI to help restore giant kelp forests.
entries.summary: Underwater forests of giant kelp protect coastlines, provide habitat, and support marine ecosystems — but they’re disappearing worldwide due to ocean warming. As COP31 k…
entries.content:
Underwater forests of giant kelp protect coastlines, provide habitat, and support marine ecosystems — but they’re disappearing worldwide due to ocean warming. As COP31 kicks off this week, we’re sharing results from our partnership with Australia's national science agency, CSIRO, which is using AI and genomics to help restore giant kelp.

The team recently published two high-quality reference genomes for Australian giant kelp, providing a foundation for conservation genetics work. Next researchers trained a version of Google's open-source AI tool DeepVariant to analyze giant kelp DNA. It sequenced 600 wild specimens collected from 40 sites along the Tasmanian coast, where populations have dwindled to 5% of historic numbers.

This video explains how the genetic analysis and partners’ lab-based cross-breeding studies are laying the groundwork for a real-world outcome: giant kelp forests replanted with diverse, heat-tolerant specimens. This effort is part of Google Australia's Digital Futures Initiative.

entries.title: Meet the 2026 Google PhD Fellows
entries.summary: A classroom lecture scene on the lower left showing students listening to an instructor, and a researcher in a lab coat working at a computer station with laboratory equipment on the upper right.
entries.content:
Today, we are announcing the recipients of the 2026 Google PhD Fellowship Program. This year, Google.org is providing $13 million in funding to support fellowship recipients, including 148 new PhD fellows across 38 countries, deepening our commitment to the early-career scientists who are advancing the "science of AI" for the public good.

The 2026 Google PhD Fellowship cohort has broad global reach, with representation across 38 countries.

Foundational science with global reach

Every transformative leap in technology begins the same way: with a researcher asking a bold, foundational question long before the rest of the world sees the answer. What makes this cohort extraordinary isn’t just the technical depth of their work, but the global reach and real-world ambition behind it. Around the world, these fellows are tackling problems that matter to communities everywhere:

  • Accelerating health and life sciences: From developing representation-learning frameworks in Brazil that integrate complex genetic data to uncover disease causes, to making medical-imaging neural networks more interpretable and reliable in South Africa.
  • Building inclusive, resilient systems: From advancing natural language processing and speech recognition for Nigerian languages, to co-designing accessible security and privacy tools for Deaf and hard-of-hearing communities in Germany.
  • Pushing the frontiers of AI and computer hardware: From designing faster microchips that process data more efficiently in Taiwan, to creating reliable, step-by-step reasoning for language models and testing quantum theory in the lab.

Direct funding and lifelong community

Breakthrough science rarely happens in isolation. Beyond direct funding and access to compute which gives students the freedom to pursue high-risk, high-reward ideas, every fellow gains access to engage with Google researchers, and is welcomed into a global scientific peer network.

Since 2009, the PhD Fellowship Program has supported more than 1,100 graduate students worldwide. Over the past 17 years, we have seen firsthand where that early catalyst can lead. Alumni of the program are now tenured professors, startup founders, open-source pioneers, and research leaders helping shape technology at Google itself.

When we support foundational science and the emerging researchers brave enough to chart the unknown, we help build a stronger, more representative global scientific landscape for everyone. Congratulations to the 2026 Google PhD Fellows. Explore the full list of 2026 recipients.

entries.title: We're launching a $10 million Energy Impact Program in West Virginia.
entries.summary: Google is launching a $10 million Energy Impact Program in West Virginia to fund home repairs and efficiency upgrades. Check your eligibility today.
entries.content:
Today, we’re announcing a $10 million Energy Impact Program to support energy innovation and affordability in West Virginia. The first $1 million will go toward the West Virginia Office of Energy across six counties: Putnam, Kanawha, Cabell, Mason, Jackson, and Lincoln.

Many older homes require basic repairs — like fixing roof leaks or outdated wiring — before they qualify for energy upgrades. This funding covers those essential repairs, helping qualifying families access the state Home Energy Rebate program to lower their monthly utility bills.

Additionally, local governments and nonprofits will receive funding through the EECBG program for lighting, insulation, and HVAC upgrades, allowing them to redirect utility savings back into local services.

This initiative is an early step in Google’s long-term investment in the communities near its planned Buffalo data center campus. To check eligibility and apply, visit energywv.org.

entries.title: Designing for privacy on intelligent eyewear
entries.summary: Google G on a blue shield. In the background are various icons related to privacy: an eye with a diagonal line over it, a gear, an off button, etc.
entries.content:
Intelligent eyewear with Gemini 1 can help you understand another language, make sense of a confusing parking sign, or know when to take the next step in your recipe, all thanks to its ability to see what you see. And with experiences like Guided Vision in Gemini Live, these glasses can provide audio descriptions to people who are blind or have low vision as they read small print or find everyday items. 2

But when technology can see the world around you, it has a responsibility to the people around you, too.

Throughout our years of research on glasses, we listened closely to wearers, bystanders, and privacy experts. We found that wearers were constantly calculating using glasses like these out-and-about during their day, while bystanders noted concerns about being filmed without their knowledge. This led us to the conviction that privacy protections on glasses must cover both the person behind the lenses and those in front of them.

Privacy designed for both sides of the lens

With this in mind, we set out to design the glasses so that personal help doesn’t come at the expense of anyone’s privacy. Here are some of the key features we’ve built into both the hardware and software to protect wearers and those nearby.

Protecting your visual data

  • Camera visuals aren’t saved in your Gemini History. When you ask Gemini on glasses about the world around you, like getting help translating a menu in another language, the camera visuals are not saved in your Gemini History. 3
  • Camera visuals aren’t used for AI training or ad targeting. The visuals Gemini captures are used to give you answers or get you the help you need. They are not used to train AI models or target ads.
  • Your data is encrypted. Data stored on glasses is encrypted, and if data leaves your glasses — like for processing on your phone or in the cloud — it’s also encrypted in transit to keep it private and secure. Coming soon, we’re also bringing Private AI Compute technology to glasses to process data in a secure, fortified space in addition to our other safeguards.

You choose what you share

  • You choose what apps can access your camera. Giving apps access to your glasses camera can be really helpful, like if you want to sync your audiobook app with the last page you read in your paperback copy. But before any app can access your camera for the first time, it asks for your permission. After that, you stay in control, and you can grant or revoke access anytime for each individual app.
  • You control your Gemini history. Your chats are saved in Gemini History so you can pick up a conversation where you left off and get more personalized help. You control your personalization and history settings, so you can review past interactions, delete individual chats, or even delete all of them. You can also control in settings whether the text of your chats is used to improve generative AI models. Learn more about how your Gemini data is handled in the Gemini Apps Privacy Hub.
  • Every pair has an off switch. And of course, you have a physical power switch on the frames to turn your glasses completely off whenever you want to wear them as regular glasses only.

Privacy protections for those around you

  • Every pair of glasses has an outer indicator light. We’ve heard from bystanders that the most helpful feature for them is a clear indication that the glasses are recording photos and videos. When you take a photo or video for your gallery, an outward-facing LED indicator lights up to let people around you know.
  • The indicator light is designed not to be messed with. If the indicator light is covered or tampered with, sensors are designed to detect that and prevent photos or videos from being taken.
  • The glasses are designed to redact faces before sending images to Gemini. When you ask Gemini a question, there may be others nearby. Not only are these Gemini visuals not used for AI model training, your glasses are also designed to automatically redact bystanders’ faces before Gemini processes the visuals.
  • Gemini is designed to focus on your voice. We’ve also designed Gemini to focus on your voice by default, and not other voices around you, using directional microphones on the glasses.

These are a few examples of the privacy features built into the intelligent eyewear experience. Learn more about our approach in the Google Safety Center.

Protections and restrictions across Google

In addition to these features, there are also protections across Google apps and services to deter misuse of the glasses.

  • Responsible use requirements: Before using intelligent eyewear, users must agree not to record others without permission, not to record in sensitive places, and not to cover the outer indicator light. Not following these requirements is a violation of the Google Terms of Service, and a user’s ability to use the glasses may be disabled.
  • Google Shopping and Google Ads: Policies do not allow the promotion of products and services that disable or hide recording indicator lights on smart glasses.
  • Google Play: Policies prohibit apps from using the camera for social live-streaming or real-time facial identification, and from changing the behavior of the outer indicator light.
  • YouTube: Policies prohibit content that depicts things like harassment and unwanted sexualization. Any video uploaded to YouTube — whether it’s recorded on a phone, a camera, or glasses — has to follow these policies, and videos that don’t are removed.
  • Account restrictions: Intelligent eyewear devices are designed to be set up only with compatible 18+ Google Accounts.

This is just the beginning. Privacy is foundational to how we design, build, and evolve wearable technology. As glasses become more capable, our focus is on creating helpful experiences that make both wearers and bystanders feel protected. We look forward to advancing this work in collaboration with privacy experts and others across the ecosystem to further protections for everyone on both sides of the lens.

entries.title: See our intelligent eyewear lineup and pre-order your pair
entries.summary: A man and two women wearing the new Warby Parker Intelligent Eyewear frames look at the camera. Along the top are Warby Parker, Google, and Samsung logos.
entries.content:
Today, pre-orders begin for the new Intelligent Eyewear collections, made in collaboration with Gentle Monster, Warby Parker, and Samsung. With help from Gemini, these frames are ready to bring you real-time assistance throughout your day, right when you need it. 1

The new Intelligent Eyewear collections

These collections, which were designed to fit a variety of styles, integrate helpful technology into frames you’ll want to wear every day, and work with Pixel and Samsung phones, as well as iPhones. 2

Gentle Monster’s high-end designs transform glasses into a means of self-expression. Their Intelligent Eyewear Collection includes six designs in bold colors — including dark red, pink, gray, and yellow — paired with tinted, clear, blue, or brown lenses. Prescription options are available for most frames. Starting at $449, the collection will be available in the United States and in South Korea.

Warby Parker’s Intelligent Eyewear lineup features three refined styles — Alden, Reid, and Wren — inspired by the brand’s most beloved silhouettes, with timeless design and lightweight comfort at the forefront. You can choose from optical or sun styles starting at $395, in Pine, Saddle, and Jet Black colorways, with a wide range of prescription, width, and lens options. The full collection is available at warbyparker.com, and customers can sign up for a guided demo experience at more than 360 Warby Parker retail locations.

Intelligent eyewear was engineered to be comfortable and helpful all day. The glasses feature lightweight frames (weighing around 41 grams) and a battery that lasts up to nine hours. 3 Each pair comes with a sleek, portable charging case that can recharge your frames up to seven times. 4

A smarter way to see the world

Gemini on intelligent eyewear helps connect the dots across the Google apps and services you use every day to get you hands-free help. Just say “Hey Gemini” or tap your frames to learn the story behind a street art mural you are passing by, ask for a tailored recommendation from a “New Arrivals” bookshelf, or look at an event poster to check your Calendar availability on the spot.

Gemini also helps handle your busywork in the background. Whether you’re walking between meetings or running errands with your hands full, you can ask Gemini to add what you’re looking at to your grocery list, or remind you where your next meeting is — all while keeping your eyes up and your day moving.

When you’re exploring somewhere new, Google Maps delivers turn-by-turn directions in your ear. And when you ask Gemini, Google Translate will deliver real-time speech translation with automatic language detection across more than 70 languages.

The glasses also feature Gemini’s new Guided Vision, which offers conversational audio descriptions to people who are blind, have low vision, or want intuitive visual assistance as they read small print or find everyday items. 5 And thanks to our collaboration with Aira, users can say “Hey Gemini, open Aira Explorer” to stream their glasses' camera feed directly to a professionally trained human visual interpreter for real-time support.

Never miss a moment

Custom-tuned open-ear speakers direct clear vocals and balanced audio right into your ear while keeping you fully aware of what’s around you. You can soundtrack your day with YouTube Music, Spotify, or Apple Music, and jump back into your audiobook on Audible. 6 Or use your glasses to catch up on your missed group chats, respond to messages, and take phone calls hands-free.

With the integrated 12-megapixel ultra-wide camera, capturing high-quality photos and videos is as simple as pressing a button — or just asking Gemini. Your phone stays in your pocket so you can capture the moment while staying in it. HDR processing and image stabilization ensure your images and videos stay crisp, vibrant, and steady, while spatial audio capture helps you relive the moments like you were there.

Privacy designed for both sides of the lens

When technology can see the world around you, it has a responsibility to the people around you, too. We set out to design intelligent eyewear so that personal help doesn’t come at the expense of anyone’s privacy.

You can read about our approach to privacy on intelligent eyewear in our blog, and learn more about privacy features on the Google Safety Center. Key protections include:

  • Camera visuals from Gemini on glasses are not saved in your Gemini History and aren’t used to train AI models or target ads. Your glasses are also designed to automatically redact bystanders’ faces from these visuals before Gemini processes them.
  • Data stored on glasses is encrypted, and if data leaves your glasses, it’s also encrypted in transit to keep it private and secure.
  • You control which apps access your glasses’ camera and mic, and you can change these permissions whenever you like. You can also review or delete your chats with Gemini, and adjust your settings at any time in Gemini History.
  • When you take a photo or video for your gallery, an indicator light lets people around you know. The glasses are designed to stop recording if the light is covered or disabled.
  • Every pair has an off switch so you can turn your glasses completely off whenever you want to wear them as regular glasses only.

Pre-orders are live online and in-store at Gentle Monster and Warby Parker. Hands-on demos are also available at select Gentle Monster, Warby Parker, and Google Store locations. Intelligent eyewear will be available to purchase in stores and online on December 10. Learn more at glasses.google.
